coverage.application_semantics: Corpus relations expose stored documentary references, including conditional theorem premises. Use project_graph arguments or query_papers prerequisites for scoped application requirements; do not recompute free assumptions from this flat record pool.
coverage.scope: All records in this captured graph, not all mathematics or merged editions. Paper subgraphs retain recorded argument prerequisites and associated records. Evidence subjects outside a paper remain in the corpus without expanding that paper's argument. Shared membership is not a paper-to-paper proof edge. Direct passages come only from explicit mapping fields; absence does not establish absence from the prose. Paper reading order is separate from mathematical dependency. Node-root traversal and typed witnesses remain available through project_graph and query_papers.

notes: Records of printed results, Lean declarations and the formalizes edges between them are copied from evidence/paper_evidence.json at 3368d1e69467aec111eb3244843ad3542171ff96; their evidence records carry the tool string "Copied from the papers' evidence mapping (plectis-paper-evidence/2); no review by this example".

Records whose ids begin step., exp.step., context., lit., open. and problem., and every supports or cites edge between records, were written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the pinned papers (authored/argument.json); each such edge has its own semantic_review record with status not_run.

Every node has status unverified, open or external: no Lean build or extraction was run by this tool, so no declaration is kernel_checked here. Builds and Comparator runs made by the repository's own GitHub Actions workflows are platform_observation records.

The two short-paper results Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 4.1 have the same statements as long-record Theorems 1.3 and 1.4 and share one record each; short Theorem 1.2 and long Theorem 1.1 differ and are separate records joined by a cites edge.
Erdős Problem #257 is open. The papers prove sufficient conditions for irrationality; none of them characterises the supports in the problem.
graph.scope: Three papers on Erdős Problem #257 by W. Cook, pinned at wcook04/plectis-erdos 3368d1e69467aec111eb3244843ad3542171ff96: the short paper, the exposition and the long record; the Lean declarations their evidence mapping cites at 436f55ebdafa67e4af0fff79f621c13f2ded12bf; and the Comparator replay of corpus commit cc7e541cf2081c6fef5a5e377d52e365e33b01eb. The problem itself remains open.
